lines.text: This hundred-dollar bill just lost twenty-three bucks. And nobody touched it.
In 2020, Sam put one hundred dollars in a drawer.
Today, it only buys what seventy-seven dollars bought back then.
Because prices are up about thirty-one percent.
A pound of coffee went from four dollars to over nine.
The bill did not shrink. Its buying power did.
To keep up, those hundred dollars would need to be one thirty-one today.
So next time someone tells you cash is safe, remember:
